bluf: Wednesday brings the highest combined threat posture since this brief was established. Karmelo Anthony was found GUILTY of murder Tuesday evening and immediately sentenced to 35 years. Crowds outside the Collin County Courthouse broke into shoving, chanting 'Free Karmelo,' and traded insults between opposing groups. Austin civil unrest risk is now at its PEAK — protests expected throughout Wednesday on Capitol/Congress Ave corridor and UT campus. Simultaneously, U.S. forces launched retaliatory strikes against Iran after Iran downed a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has retaliated against U.S. Fifth Fleet (Bahrain), a U.S. airbase in Jordan, and Kuwait — this is an active armed conflict. FIFA World Cup opens TOMORROW (June 11) — Iranian diaspora tensions are now at their absolute peak given the military conflict; cyber posture is HIGH. Heat index 98–102°F today. All senior staff should be briefed before morning shift. Emergency escalation protocols on standby.

incidents.title: Karmelo Anthony — GUILTY VERDICT + 35-Year Sentence (Post-Verdict Day)
incidents.location: Collin County Courthouse, McKinney TX / Austin-wide protest watch
incidents.detail: Karmelo Anthony, 19, was found GUILTY of murder Tuesday evening by a Collin County jury after deliberating less than three hours. He was immediately sentenced to 35 years in prison. The jury rejected his self-defense claim — Anthony never testified and defense rested without a single witness substantiating self-defense. Crowd outside the courthouse broke into shoving, chanting, and emotional confrontations immediately after the verdict was announced. Anthony supporters chanted 'Free Karmelo'; opposing groups celebrated the verdict and called for justice for Austin Metcalf. Deputies stood by monitoring the scene. WEDNESDAY AUSTIN RISK: Post-verdict is historically the highest demonstration day. Civil rights groups had pre-positioned protest activity for any verdict. A guilty verdict with a 35-year sentence is considered by many social justice advocates as disproportionate — all-white jury controversy intensifies the anger. PRIORITY WATCH ZONES: Texas State Capitol grounds, Congress Ave, UT West Mall, 6th Street. Exterior staff must not engage demonstrators. Contact APD non-emergency (512-974-5000) if any crowd exceeds 50 persons within one block of 98 San Jacinto Blvd. Maintain HIGH posture all day.
incidents.source: CNN / ABC News / Dallas Morning News / Fox News

incidents.title: U.S.–Iran Active Armed Conflict — U.S. Strikes Southern Iran; Iran Retaliates
incidents.location: Middle East / Bahrain / Jordan / Kuwait (national; diaspora monitor Austin)
incidents.detail: ESCALATION CONFIRMED: Iran downed a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz on June 9. Both crew members were rescued in a nighttime special operations mission. U.S. CENTCOM launched 'self-defense strikes' against Iranian targets in southern Iran in retaliation. Iran's IRGC then struck: U.S. Fifth Fleet Headquarters in Bahrain; U.S. airbase in Jordan; Kuwait (nature of strikes TBD as of 5 AM). This is an active armed conflict between U.S. and Iran — the previous ceasefire has collapsed. Trump spoke with press defending the strikes as 'very powerful.' AUSTIN RELEVANCE (HIGH): Iranian diaspora community in Austin's tech sector is now deeply alarmed — combination of WC team staging in Tijuana, the military strikes, and the WC opening tomorrow (June 11). Expect heightened emotions in any Iranian community gatherings. FIFA WC security posture escalates to its highest level. DHS and FBI will have activated emergency protocols at all WC host cities. Austin is NOT a host city but luxury hospitality targets remain elevated. Brief all staff on avoiding geopolitical conversation with guests. Any suspicious activity or inquiries about U.S. military operations should be logged.
incidents.source: Al Jazeera / CBS News / ABC News / Fox News / NYT

civil_unrest.title: Karmelo Anthony Post-Verdict — Austin Protest Risk: ACTIVE HIGH
civil_unrest.location: Capitol/Congress Ave / UT Campus / Downtown Austin
civil_unrest.detail: Post-verdict Wednesday is the highest-risk day for Austin demonstrations in this cycle. The 35-year sentence with an all-white jury has social media on fire — 'Free Karmelo' is trending. Civil rights groups had pre-positioned mobilization for either verdict outcome; a guilty verdict with a long sentence is more likely to drive sustained street action than an acquittal would have. Expect rallies at Capitol grounds, marching on Congress Ave, and possible convergence toward 6th Street in the evening. No confirmed permitted march in Austin as of 5 AM — expect spontaneous gathering. Monitor X, Telegram, Instagram for Austin-specific organizing keywords. KEY PROTOCOL: If crowd approaches within 2 blocks of 98 San Jacinto Blvd, lock down secondary entrances, post additional staff at lobby doors, notify APD. Do NOT engage demonstrators. Protect guests' movement safely.
